*   **Inputs:** Two scalar distance values $a$ and $b$ (the SDF values at a query point for two primitives), and a blending radius parameter $k$ (or $r$) [Object Combination Operators](1801-object-combination-operators.md).

*   **Lipschitz Continuity:** Standard smooth minimums can violate the Lipschitz condition (gradient magnitude > 1) when combining SDFs, leading to ray marching artifacts [Object Combination Operators](1801-object-combination-operators.md).
These operators preserve Lipschitz continuity provided the gradients of the two SDFs are at right angles (orthogonal) [Object Combination Operators](1801-object-combination-operators.md).

*   **Gradient Misalignment:** If the gradients are off by more than 30 degrees, or if the surfaces are parallel and close to each other, the Lipschitz condition may no longer hold, causing artifacts [Object Combination Operators](1801-object-combination-operators.md).

*   **Parameter Scale:** The parameter $r$ (or $k$) must be significantly smaller than the size of the objects to maintain validity [Object Combination Operators](1801-object-combination-operators.md).
*   **Parallel Surfaces:** The operator assumes intersecting or adjacent surfaces with distinct normals.
Parallel surfaces may produce incorrect distances [Object Combination Operators](1801-object-combination-operators.md).
*   **Measured Performance:** Not given in the sources.

*   **Limitations:** Does not preserve exact distance values (it is an approximation); Lipschitz continuity is not guaranteed for non-orthogonal gradients or parallel surfaces, leading to ray marching artifacts [Object Combination Operators](1801-object-combination-operators.md).
The method is a key component of Constructive SDF Modeling, allowing for the creation of complex scenes from simple primitives [Object Combination Operators](1801-object-combination-operators.md).
